reviewScope: Black Whale vessel, spatial, access, operational, structural and scale evidence only

pass1.method: Full-page visual sweep of all 19 ordered pages

pass2.method: Full-resolution verification of numbered royal-suite thresholds 1001–1014, suite interiors, repeated corridor fronts, room-use states and the lower-tier industrial crowd compartment

retainedPanels.subject: Room 1013 threshold and interior
retainedPanels.visualDescription: The 1013 plaque sits above a tall decorated suite entrance; the room beyond contains a large table, several standing guards and broad finished floor space.
modelingPermissions: Register Room 1013 as a corridor-facing royal suite with a large furnished interior
modelingProhibitions: Do not infer exact dimensions or adjacency beyond the shown corridor sequence

retainedPanels.subject: Room 1010 overhead room view
retainedPanels.visualDescription: An elevated view into Room 1010 shows a broad furnished floor, multiple occupants and a doorway edge, providing a useful occupancy and zoning reference.
modelingPermissions: Use the panel as a room-scale and furniture-density constraint
modelingProhibitions: Do not trace the panel as a metrically exact floor plan

retainedPanels.subject: Room 1003 large table interior
retainedPanels.visualDescription: Room 1003 contains a long central table surrounded by standing guards and attendants with open circulation around the furniture.
modelingPermissions: Represent Room 1003 as a large furnished meeting-capable suite

retainedPanels.subject: Room 1002 dining area
retainedPanels.visualDescription: The 1002 suite shows a formal dining table with place settings and two seated occupants within a decorated enclosed room.
modelingPermissions: Register a formal dining-use zone in Room 1002 as a chapter state
modelingProhibitions: Do not assume the dining arrangement is permanent or exhausts the suite plan

retainedPanels.subject: Room 1014 corridor threshold
retainedPanels.visualDescription: The 1014 plaque is mounted above a tall decorated doorway opening to a broad royal corridor occupied by several guards.
modelingPermissions: Register Room 1014 on the repeated royal-suite corridor system
modelingProhibitions: Do not derive exact distance to neighboring numbered suites from montage order

retainedPanels.subject: Lower-tier industrial crowd compartment 37564
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A dense crowd occupies a large utilitarian compartment beneath exposed beams, pipes and ceiling services, with a prominent 37564 sign overhead.
modelingPermissions: Represent a large lower-tier communal compartment with exposed overhead services and dense temporary occupancy
modelingProhibitions: Do not interpret 37564 as a room count, population total or deck coordinate without independent confirmation

evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1013 threshold and large-room class.

evidence.claim: Room 1012 has a visible numeric plaque above a tall decorated entrance and an enclosed furnished interior.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1012 threshold identity.

evidence.claim: Room 1011 is marked at a corridor-facing entrance and contains a bed-centered private interior.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1011 as a private royal-suite interior without fixing its full plan.

evidence.claim: Room 1010 is visibly labeled and shown from an elevated angle with broad floor area, furniture and several occupants.
evidence.modelingUse: Use as a room-scale and zoning reference only.

evidence.claim: Room 1009 is identified by signage and shown as a furnished occupied suite rather than a corridor or public hall.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1009 threshold and enclosed-suite class.

evidence.claim: Room 1008 has a visible plaque and a corridor-facing doorway with guards and attendants gathered nearby.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1008 on the guarded royal corridor system.

evidence.claim: Room 1007 is marked above a tall entrance and contains formal seating and a table.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1007 threshold and furnished reception-use state.

evidence.claim: Room 1006 is identified at a decorated doorway while a book and nearby occupants establish an occupied private suite context.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1006 threshold; keep object placement temporal.

evidence.claim: Room 1005 has a visible plaque and a formal desk-centered interior with several guards.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1005 as a large working or audience-use room state.

evidence.claim: Room 1004 is visibly labeled at a corridor-facing front with guards stationed around its entrance.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1004 guarded threshold.

evidence.claim: Room 1003 is labeled and contains a long central table with open circulation around standing occupants.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1003 large meeting-capable interior.

evidence.claim: Repeated decorated wall fields, tall doorways and guard clusters continue across the royal residential corridor.
evidence.modelingUse: Reinforce the repeated-suite-front corridor type without exact spacing.

evidence.claim: Groups can stand and converse in the royal corridor while leaving a usable passage between suite fronts.
evidence.modelingUse: Constrain the corridor to a broad circulation class.

evidence.claim: Room 1002 is visibly labeled and used as a formal dining room with a central table and place settings.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1002 dining-use chapter state.

evidence.claim: A decorated royal room supports seated conversation, furniture and clear circulation to a doorway.
evidence.modelingUse: Retain enclosed furnished-suite scale; room identity remains contextual.

evidence.claim: Room 1001 is marked above a tall decorated doorway and contains a private occupied interior.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1001 threshold and suite identity.

evidence.claim: Room 1014 is visibly labeled above a corridor-facing entrance with several guards in the surrounding passage.
evidence.modelingUse: Register Room 1014 on the guarded royal corridor system.

evidence.claim: A broad formal room accommodates a table, numerous standing guards and seated occupants across open floor.
evidence.modelingUse: Reinforce large-room occupancy and circulation class.

evidence.claim: A dense crowd occupies a large utilitarian ship compartment under exposed beams, pipes and ceiling services beside a 37564 sign.
evidence.modelingUse: Register a lower-tier communal industrial-space class and quarantine the sign meaning.

evidence.claim: The chapter confirms a complete set of visible royal-suite labels from 1001 through 1014, but does not prove their exact geometric order.
evidence.modelingUse: Use the labels as identity nodes only; topology requires independent corridor evidence.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Numbered-suite montage order
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: The chapter surveys rooms 1013 through 1001 and 1014, but editorial order does not prove exact physical adjacency, direction or bay spacing.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Suite furniture and occupancy
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: Tables, chairs, beds, guards and attendants are chapter-state contents and must not be frozen as permanent architecture.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Sign 37564
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: The sign is confirmed in a lower-tier crowd compartment, but its numbering system and semantic meaning remain unknown.

unresolvedQuestions: Does the 1001–1014 numbering correspond to physical corridor order or only prince assignment?
Which royal suites share the same corridor segment and which are separated by turns or lobbies?
What system does the lower-tier sign 37564 encode?

categories: Nen and succession strategy retained only where panels independently show ship space
character motives and dialogue without additional spatial content
